arguments.sql_query:
WITH immuno AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ca.descendant_concept_id AS concept_id
  FROM omop.concept_ancestor ca
  WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id = 21603890 -- ATC L04 Immunosuppressants
), yearly AS (
  SELECT
    YEAR(de.drug_exposure_start_date) AS yr,
    COUNT(*) AS total_drug_exposures,
    COUNT(DISTINCT de.person_id) AS persons_with_any_drug,
    SUM(CASE WHEN i.concept_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS immuno_exposures,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN i.concept_id IS NOT NULL THEN de.person_id END) AS persons_with_immuno
  FROM omop.drug_exposure de
  LEFT JOIN immuno i ON de.drug_concept_id = i.concept_id
  WHERE de.drug_exposure_start_date >= '2019-01-01'
    AND de.drug_exposure_start_date < '2021-01-01'
  GROUP BY YEAR(de.drug_exposure_start_date)
)
SELECT
  yr,
  total_drug_exposures,
  persons_with_any_drug,
  immuno_exposures,
  persons_with_immuno,
  CAST(1000.0 * immuno_exposures / NULLIF(total_drug_exposures,0) AS DECIMAL(12,3)) AS immuno_rx_per_1000_drug_exposures,
  CAST(1000.0 * persons_with_immuno / NULLIF(persons_with_any_drug,0) AS DECIMAL(12,3)) AS immuno_patients_per_1000_drug_patients
FROM yearly
ORDER BY yr;

content.text: The first full scan timed out, so I’ll narrow it into separate indexed year-level queries.

arguments.sql_query: SELECT YEAR(drug_exposure_start_date) AS yr, COUNT(*) AS total_drug_exposures, COUNT(DISTINCT person_id) AS persons_with_any_drug FROM omop.drug_exposure WHERE drug_exposure_start_date >= '2019-01-01' AND drug_exposure_start_date < '2021-01-01' GROUP BY YEAR(drug_exposure_start_date) ORDER BY yr
SELECT COUNT(*) AS l04_descendant_concepts FROM omop.concept_ancestor WHERE ancestor_concept_id = 21603890

WITH immuno AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT descendant_concept_id AS drug_concept_id
  FROM omop.concept_ancestor
  WHERE ancestor_concept_id = 21603890
)
SELECT YEAR(de.drug_exposure_start_date) AS yr,
       COUNT(*) AS immuno_exposures,
       COUNT(DISTINCT de.person_id) AS persons_with_immuno
FROM omop.drug_exposure de
JOIN immuno i ON i.drug_concept_id = de.drug_concept_id
WHERE de.drug_exposure_start_date >= '2019-01-01'
  AND de.drug_exposure_start_date < '2021-01-01'
GROUP BY YEAR(de.drug_exposure_start_date)
ORDER BY yr

content.text: I found higher raw counts in 2020, but “rate” depends on denominator. I’ll also check active-patient denominators from observation periods.

arguments.sql_query:
SELECT y.yr, COUNT(DISTINCT op.person_id) AS active_persons
FROM (SELECT 2019 AS yr, CAST('2019-01-01' AS date) AS start_dt, CAST('2019-12-31' AS date) AS end_dt
      UNION ALL SELECT 2020, CAST('2020-01-01' AS date), CAST('2020-12-31' AS date)) y
JOIN omop.observation_period op
  ON op.observation_period_start_date <= y.end_dt
 AND op.observation_period_end_date >= y.start_dt
GROUP BY y.yr
ORDER BY y.yr

content.text:
Yes — using ATC `L04 Immunosuppressants` as systemic immunosuppressants, the **rate declined in 2020 vs 2019**, even though absolute counts increased.

| Year | Immunosuppressant prescriptions | Total drug exposures | Rate per 1,000 drug exposures | Patients with immunosuppressant | Rate per 1,000 patients with any drug |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2019 | 243,677 | 20,175,039 | 12.08 | 12,602 | 30.46 |
| 2020 | 272,184 | 24,069,739 | 11.31 | 13,627 | 15.08 |

Interpretation:
- **Prescription-volume rate declined**: 12.08 → 11.31 per 1,000 drug exposures, about a **6.4% relative decrease**.
- **Patient-level rate declined more strongly** among patients with any drug exposure: 30.46 → 15.08 per 1,000, about a **50.5% relative decrease**.
- Absolute immunosuppressant prescriptions increased, so the decline is specifically in the **rate/proportion**, not the count.

Caveat: I used `drug_exposure` and OMOP ATC ancestor concept `L04`; an observation-period denominator query timed out, so this is normalized to drug-exposure and drug-treated-patient denominators.
